ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a Zener diode voltage regulator circuit. The left-side power supply is labeled V_source = 15 V, and the power supply is connected through the upper series resistor R_series to the output node; the series resistor is labeled 500 Ω. This output node is connected downward through a Zener diode to ground, and the Zener voltage is labeled V_z = 5.1 V; on the right side of the same node, a load resistor R_load is also connected in parallel to ground. Reasoning calculation: The Zener diode clamps the output node at 5.1 V. The series resistor current is I_series = (15 - 5.1) / 500 = 9.9 / 500 = 0.0198 A = 19.8 mA. Given R_load = 330 Ω, the load current is I_load = 5.1 / 330 = 0.01545 A = 15.45 mA. The node current distribution is I_series = I_load + I_zener, therefore I_zener = 19.8 - 15.45 = 4.35 mA.
